GameComposer.placeholder: Describe the game you want to build…

pro.label: Pro
pro.tagline: Slower and stronger, for mechanics that need real reasoning.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.tagline: Fast and capable. The right pick for most games.

fast.label: Fast
fast.tagline: Cheapest and quickest, for small tweaks and quick iterations.

voxelSurvival.label: Voxel survival
voxelSurvival.prompt: Build a first-person voxel survival game: mine and place blocks in a world I can walk around, gather what I need before nightfall, and stay alive.

inkSamuraiDuel.label: Ink samurai duel
inkSamuraiDuel.prompt: Build a one-on-one samurai duel in a black-and-white ink-wash style, where fights are won by timing a parry and the counter-strike that follows it.

comicBookFirefight.label: Comic-book firefight
comicBookFirefight.prompt: Build a top-down firefight drawn like a comic book — bold outlines, halftone shading and onomatopoeia popping up on every hit — where I clear a room of enemies using cover.

realisticBattlefield.label: Realistic battlefield
realisticBattlefield.prompt: Build a first-person battlefield sequence with a realistic look: cross open ground under fire, use cover, and take an objective.

fightFirstShooter.label: Fight-first shooter
fightFirstShooter.prompt: Build an arena shooter that rewards pushing forward rather than hiding: health comes from killing, enemies pressure me constantly, and standing still is what gets me killed.

jungleExpeditionDrive.label: Jungle expedition drive
jungleExpeditionDrive.prompt: Build a driving game through dense jungle: an off-road route with mud, river crossings and steep climbs where keeping the vehicle intact matters as much as speed.

sunnyKingdomPlatformer.label: Sunny kingdom platformer
sunnyKingdomPlatformer.prompt: Build a bright 3D platformer set in a sunny storybook kingdom: run, jump and double-jump across floating islands to collect what is scattered across each one.

Pricing.faqWhatIsCreditAnswer: One credit is one US cent of what a turn costs to generate. Building a game is a conversation with a model, and a long conversation about a complicated game costs more than a short one about a simple game — so credits are spent by the turn rather than by the game.
Pricing.faqUsageAnswer: Every turn reports what it actually used when it finishes, and that is what comes off your balance. Nothing is charged up front and nothing is estimated, so a turn that fails costs you nothing. Balances settle a few seconds behind the turn that moved them, which is why the number in the sidebar can lag a refresh or two.
Pricing.faqRunningOutQuestion: What happens when I run out?
Pricing.faqRunningOutAnswer: New turns stop until your balance recovers. Nothing is deleted and nothing is locked: every game you have already built stays yours to open, play and share. Free plans refill on the first of the month, and Pro or Max plans can buy a top-up without waiting.
Pricing.faqRolloverAnswer: Monthly credits do not. Whatever is left of your Free, Pro or Max allowance expires when the month does, and a fresh allowance arrives in its place. Top-up credits are the exception: they never expire, and they are only touched once the month’s allowance is gone.
Pricing.faqTopUpPlanQuestion: Why do top-ups need a paid plan?
Pricing.faqTopUpPlanAnswer: Top-up credits never expire, so on their own they would be a pay-as-you-go plan nobody designed — cheaper for the buyer than either plan and lumpier for us than either plan. They exist as a release valve for a heavy month on top of a subscription, which is the only shape in which both sides of that trade work.
Pricing.faqSwitchPlansQuestion: What happens when I switch between Pro and Max?
Pricing.faqSwitchPlansAnswer: Moving up to Max charges the prorated difference right away and switches your credits immediately. Moving down to Pro takes effect at the start of your next billing cycle, so a month you already paid the Max price for keeps its Max allowance.
Pricing.faqCancelQuestion: Can I cancel whenever I want?
Pricing.faqCancelAnswer: Yes. A cancelled Pro or Max plan runs to the end of the period you have already paid for, then drops to Free. Any top-up credits you bought survive that, because they were never tied to the subscription.
